Thanks Tracy — great questions. Quick answers inline, and looping Sean (network engineering) to add the technical details: 

1) Scale: We recommend Dedicated if you're planning sustained 400 rps at 256 tokens — Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved GPU pools. Private VPC can autoscale with Dedicated under the hood (Redwood Dedicated + Private VPC) so you can get both isolation and scale; Sean, can you confirm how the autoscale handoff looks?

2) PrivateLink & streaming: PrivateLink works with streaming. There's some additional per-GB data charging on AWS for interface endpoints; we'll include a short cost note in the one-pager. The streaming endpoint is supported over PrivateLink (we proxy SSE over the endpoint).

3) IP allowlist: For customers using allowlists for outbound firewall rules, we provide a small set of static egress IPs for control-plane and a documented range for data-plane. If you're doing inbound allowlisting to a PrivateLink endpoint, you won't need to add Redwood egress IPs — access happens over the VPC endpoint connection.

Jordan — can you share: 
- a basic diagram in the Drive link (thanks)
- AWS account ID for endpoints
- any existing NAT Gateway egress IPs you'd like us to avoid

I'll also attach a short technical checklist that Sean can fill out with the exact CIDRs and endpoint names.

Marissa

Attachments referenced: acme_network_diagram.png

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>

Hi Tracy / Jordan — Sean from Redwood infra. Thanks for the diagram Jordan, that helps a lot. I've attached a one-page checklist and an example CloudFormation snippet we often use to provision the interface endpoint and the route table updates. Quick notes: 

- Autoscale model: If you choose Private VPC + Dedicated, we pin a dedicated GPU pool and set autoscale thresholds; failover routes to our hosted pools if capacity is constrained (per SLA/rollout policy).
- Streaming: Confirmed — SSE and HTTP/2 streaming are supported over PrivateLink. We recommend enabling enhanced keepalives on your LB for long-lived connections.
- Egress IPs / allowlist: I can provide a short list of our control-plane egress IPs (3 addresses) and a recommended /24 for data-plane; if you need exact CIDRs I'll include them in the checklist.
- TLS & KMS: We support customer-managed KMS for payload encryption at rest; if you'd like, we can add the KMS key ARN to the SOW.

Next steps from infra:
- I'll review the Drive diagram and add inline comments by EOD Thu 2026-09-03.
